messages.vuln.cvss.note: What an attack needs, read from the CVSS vector.

vuln.cvss.av.N: Network: the attacker only needs to reach it over the network
vuln.cvss.av.A: Adjacent: only from a nearby network, such as the same LAN segment or Bluetooth range
vuln.cvss.av.L: Local: needs a local or SSH session, or a user tricked into acting on the machine
vuln.cvss.av.P: Physical: needs physical access to the device

vuln.cvss.ac.L: Low: no special conditions; the attacker can expect repeatable success
vuln.cvss.ac.H: High: success depends on conditions outside the attacker's control, such as gathering details of the target or winning a race

vuln.cvss.ac4.L: Low: no target-specific security measures to get around
vuln.cvss.ac4.H: High: the attacker must evade or get around security measures such as ASLR or DEP, or obtain target-specific secrets

vuln.cvss.at.N: None: success does not depend on how the target is deployed or running
vuln.cvss.at.P: Present: success depends on specific deployment or execution conditions, such as a race condition, a non-default setting or a position on the network path

vuln.cvss.pr.N: None: no account or authorization needed

vuln.cvss.ui.N: None: no action by anyone other than the attacker
vuln.cvss.ui.R: Required: a user must do something, such as open a file or click a link

vuln.cvss.ui4.N: None: no action by anyone other than the attacker
vuln.cvss.ui4.P: Passive: limited, involuntary interaction, such as visiting a page
vuln.cvss.ui4.A: Active: a user must deliberately do something specific, such as install or run a file or dismiss a warning

vuln.cvss.av2.L: Local: needs physical access or a local (shell) account
vuln.cvss.av2.A: Adjacent network: only from the same broadcast or collision domain
vuln.cvss.av2.N: Network: the attacker only needs to reach it over the network

vuln.cvss.ac2.H: High: specialized conditions, such as a narrow race window or an uncommon configuration
vuln.cvss.ac2.M: Medium: somewhat specialized conditions, such as a non-default configuration or a limited group of targets

vuln.cvss.au.M: Multiple: the attacker must authenticate two or more times
vuln.cvss.au.S: Single: one authentication, such as one login

messages.about.hot.h2: Ordering and pinning on the home page
messages.about.hot.order: The home list ({home}) is ordered by when each vulnerability last reached a new stage, newest first. For each kind of lifecycle event nday takes its earliest known time, and the latest of those times places the vulnerability; on equal times the one at the higher current stage comes first.
messages.about.hot.repeat: Once a kind of event has a known time, further events of that kind, such as another advisory with a patch or another PoC, never move the vulnerability up again. Events whose time is unknown (the source gave none and nday did not observe them live) do not count as a change.
messages.about.hot.window: By default the list covers the last {window} and only vulnerabilities whose latest change is to {stage} or a later stage, so a newly published CVE alone does not appear; {since} and {min_stage} change this. CVE records marked REJECTED are left out unless {rejected} is on.

about.hot.pin.one: On the first page, nday pins at most one vulnerability that researchers are discussing right now above the list. It is pinned only when all of the following hold.
about.hot.pin.other: On the first page, nday pins up to {max} vulnerabilities that researchers are discussing right now above the list. A vulnerability is pinned only when all of the following hold.

about.hot.pin_count.one: At least one researcher on nday's list posted about it on X in the last {window}.

about.hot.pin_recent.other: Its latest researcher post is at most {hours} hours old.

about.hot.pin_wave.one: Its current wave of discussion began at most one day ago. A wave is a run of posts with no gap longer than one day: a vulnerability discussed again after a longer silence can be pinned again, and one discussed without such a break stops being pinned one day after its wave began.
about.hot.pin_wave.other: Its current wave of discussion began at most {days} days ago. A wave is a run of posts with no gap longer than {days} days: a vulnerability discussed again after a longer silence can be pinned again, and one discussed without such a break stops being pinned {days} days after its wave began.

messages.about.hot.pin_filter: It would be in the list you are viewing anyway: same window, minimum stage, rejected switch and tags.
messages.about.hot.pin_order: Pinned rows are ordered by the number of researchers, then by the latest post. If fewer qualify than the limit, the rest is filled from the top of the discussed ranking, whatever the window or minimum stage. Pinned rows appear only on the first page and are not repeated among the ordinary rows.

tag.desc.command-injection: Untrusted input ends up in an operating-system command or its arguments.
tag.desc.code-injection: Untrusted input is evaluated as code by the application, including expression-language injection.
tag.desc.sql-injection: Untrusted input changes the meaning of a SQL query.
tag.desc.deserialization: The application deserializes untrusted data, which can lead to object injection or code execution.
tag.desc.template-injection: Untrusted input is evaluated by a server-side template engine.
tag.desc.file-upload: Files of a dangerous type can be uploaded, often leading to code execution.
tag.desc.file-inclusion: A file path or URL the attacker controls is included and executed (local or remote file inclusion).
tag.desc.path-traversal: A crafted path reaches files or directories outside the intended location.
tag.desc.ssrf: The server can be made to send requests to destinations the attacker chooses.
tag.desc.xxe: An XML parser resolves external entities, exposing files or internal services.
tag.desc.auth-bypass: Authentication can be bypassed or spoofed, or a critical function has none.
tag.desc.broken-access-control: Authorization checks are missing or wrong, so users reach data or actions they should not.
tag.desc.privilege-management: Privileges are assigned, kept or dropped incorrectly, which enables privilege escalation.
tag.desc.hardcoded-credentials: Passwords, keys or default credentials are built into the product.
tag.desc.buffer-overflow: Memory is written outside the bounds of a buffer (stack or heap overflow, out-of-bounds write).
tag.desc.use-after-free: Memory is used after it has been freed.
tag.desc.double-free: The same memory is freed twice.
tag.desc.out-of-bounds-read: Memory is read outside the bounds of a buffer.
tag.desc.type-confusion: An object is accessed as an incompatible type.
tag.desc.integer-overflow: An integer calculation wraps around or underflows.
tag.desc.format-string: Untrusted input is used as a format string.
tag.desc.uninitialized-memory: Memory, a variable or a pointer is used before it is initialized.
tag.desc.null-dereference: A NULL pointer is dereferenced, which usually crashes the process.
tag.desc.race-condition: Concurrent access to a shared resource is not synchronized correctly, including time-of-check to time-of-use gaps.
tag.desc.xss: Untrusted input runs as script in another user's browser.
tag.desc.csrf: A forged request from another site is accepted as the user's own.
tag.desc.prototype-pollution: Untrusted input modifies JavaScript object prototypes.
tag.desc.request-smuggling: Front-end and back-end servers disagree on where an HTTP request ends.
tag.desc.crlf-injection: Line breaks in input inject HTTP headers or log lines.
tag.desc.open-redirect: The application redirects to a URL the attacker chooses.
tag.desc.ui-spoofing: The user interface misrepresents what the user sees or clicks, including clickjacking.
tag.desc.search-path: Programs or libraries are loaded from a search path the attacker controls (for example DLL hijacking).
tag.desc.link-following: A symbolic or hard link makes the program access an unintended file.
tag.desc.session-management: Session identifiers can be fixed by an attacker or stay valid for too long.
tag.desc.crypto-failure: Cryptography is missing, weak or misused, certificates are not validated, or credentials are stored or sent unprotected.
tag.desc.info-disclosure: Sensitive information is exposed to people who should not see it.
tag.desc.resource-exhaustion: Uncontrolled use of CPU, memory or other resources allows denial of service.
tag.desc.remote-unauth: Reachable over the network with no authentication and no user interaction (CVSS v4.0/v3.x AV:N, PR:N and UI:N).
tag.desc.network: The attack vector is the network (CVSS AV:N).
tag.desc.adjacent: The attacker must be on an adjacent network, such as the same LAN or Bluetooth range (CVSS AV:A).
tag.desc.local: The attacker needs local access, or must get a user to run something locally (CVSS AV:L).
tag.desc.physical: The attacker needs physical access to the device (CVSS AV:P).
tag.desc.no-auth: No privileges or authentication are required (CVSS PR:N; in CVSS 2.0, Au:N).
tag.desc.no-interaction: No action by a user is required (CVSS v4.0/v3.x UI:N; CVSS 2.0 has no such metric).
tag.desc.ransomware: CISA's KEV catalog says the vulnerability is known to be used in ransomware campaigns.
tag.desc.metasploit: A Metasploit Framework module exists for this CVE.
tag.desc.exploit-db: Exploit-DB lists an exploit or proof of concept for this CVE.
tag.desc.nuclei: A nuclei template exists that detects or checks this CVE.

messages.rules.title: Community rules
messages.rules.description: The rules for the discussions on nday vulnerability pages.
messages.rules.about: Comments on vulnerability pages follow these rules:
messages.rules.contact: To appeal a moderation decision, or for anything the report button does not cover, write to {email}.
messages.rules.r1.title: Stay on the vulnerability.
messages.rules.r1.body: A discussion belongs to the CVE on its page: technical details, affected versions, patches and mitigations, detection, references.
messages.rules.r2.title: Public information only.
messages.rules.r2.body: You may link to or quote PoCs, write-ups and advisories that are already public. Do not disclose new vulnerabilities here; report them to the vendor or a coordinator first.
messages.rules.r3.title: No help attacking systems you are not authorized to test.
messages.rules.r3.body: No requests or offers for targets, access, stolen data or exploitation as a service.
messages.rules.r4.title: No personal data and no secrets.
messages.rules.r4.body: No credentials, tokens, breach data, or details that identify private individuals.
messages.rules.r5.title: Be civil.
messages.rules.r5.body: Criticize the work, not the person. No harassment, no hate, no advertising or spam.
messages.rules.r6.title: Say how you know.
messages.rules.r6.body: Cite sources, mark speculation as speculation, and say so when you write about your own or your employer's product.
messages.rules.r7.title: Moderation.
messages.rules.r7.body: Comments appear immediately. Moderators may hide comments and suspend accounts that break these rules. Use “report” on a comment to flag it.
messages.rules.r8.title: Your comments stay.
messages.rules.r8.body: They are public. You can edit or delete them. If you delete your account, your comments remain without your name.

admin.set.desc.NDAY_CVELIST_BOOTSTRAP_DAYS: How many days of CVE record changes the cvelist collector reads on its first run, before it has a cursor. 0–30, default 7.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_CVELIST_MAX_FILES: Most CVE record files cvelist fetches in one run; the rest stays queued for the next run. At least 1, default 1000.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_CVELIST_BACKFILL_RETRY_DAYS: A CVE that another source mentions but the CVE list lacks is not looked up again for this many days. 0 or more, default 7.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_GHSA_BOOTSTRAP_DAYS: How many days of GitHub advisories the ghsa collector reads on its first run. 0–90, default 7.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_GHSA_MAX_REQUESTS: Most GitHub API requests ghsa makes in one run. At least 1, default 10.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_GHSA_OVERLAP_MINUTES: Each ghsa run starts this many minutes before its last cursor, to catch advisories that appear late. 0 or more, default 60.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_GITHUB_TOKEN: GitHub token of the ghsa collector: authenticated requests get a far higher rate limit. Unset, it reads anonymously.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_X_BEARER_TOKEN: X API bearer token: the xposts collector reads posts with it and the site looks up handles on /admin/x. Unset, neither works.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_DISCUSS: Discussions on vulnerability pages, on or off (off: the discussion routes are not mounted). Default on; applies after a restart.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_DISCUSS_POST_BURST: Comments an established account may post in a row before the interval below applies. 1–100000, default 5.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_DISCUSS_POST_EVERY: After its burst, an established account may post one comment per this interval. 1ms–30d, default 30s.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_DISCUSS_POST_DAILY: Most comments an established account may post in 24 hours. 1–100000, default 60.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_DISCUSS_NEW_POST_BURST: Comments a new account may post in a row. 1–100000, default 2.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_DISCUSS_NEW_POST_EVERY: After its burst, a new account may post one comment per this interval. 1ms–30d, default 2m.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_DISCUSS_NEW_POST_DAILY: Most comments a new account may post in 24 hours. 1–100000, default 10.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_DISCUSS_NEW_ACCOUNT_AGE: An account counts as new while it is younger than this (or has too few visible comments, see the next setting). 1ms–30d, default 24h.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_DISCUSS_NEW_ACCOUNT_COMMENTS: An account counts as new while it has fewer visible comments than this. 1–100000, default 3.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_DISCUSS_ADDR_BURST: New comments from one client address, all accounts together, in a row. 1–100000, default 10.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_DISCUSS_ADDR_EVERY: After that burst, one new comment per client address per this interval. 1ms–30d, default 10s.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_DISCUSS_EDIT_BURST: Comment edits a user may make in a row. 1–100000, default 20.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_DISCUSS_EDIT_EVERY: After the edit burst, one edit per this interval (about 20 an hour by default). 1ms–30d, default 3m.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_DISCUSS_REPORT_DAILY: Most reports a user may file in 24 hours. 1–100000, default 20.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_DISCUSS_REPORT_BURST: Report requests a user may send in a row, whatever their outcome. 1–100000, default 5.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_DISCUSS_REPORT_EVERY: After the report burst, one report request per this interval. 1ms–30d, default 1m.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_DISCUSS_DELETE_BURST: Delete requests a user may send in a row (suspended users included). 1–100000, default 10.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_DISCUSS_DELETE_EVERY: After the delete burst, one delete request per this interval. 1ms–30d, default 30s.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_DISCUSS_READ_BURST: Discussion reads from one client address in a row. 1–100000, default 120.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_DISCUSS_READ_EVERY: After the read burst, one read per client address per this interval. 1ms–30d, default 500ms.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_DISCUSS_MOD_BURST: Moderation requests a moderator may send in a row. 1–100000, default 600.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_DISCUSS_MOD_EVERY: After the moderation burst, one request per this interval. 1ms–30d, default 100ms.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_DISCUSS_DUPLICATE_WINDOW: A comment repeating the author's own text on the same vulnerability within this window is refused. 1ms–30d, default 10m.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_DISCUSS_GUEST_READ: Whether signed-out visitors can read the comments on vulnerability pages, on or off (off: they see only the outline of the discussion and a call to sign in). Posting always needs an account. Default on.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_DISCUSS_GUEST_READ_BURST: How many times one client address may read comments while signed out before the interval below applies, on top of the read limit above. 1–100000, default 60.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_DISCUSS_GUEST_READ_EVERY: After that burst, how often one client address may read comments while signed out. 1ms–30d, default 2s.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_AUTH_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID: Client ID of the GitHub OAuth app; GitHub sign-in is on once it and the client secret are both set. 1–512 printable ASCII characters, no spaces.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_AUTH_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID: Client ID of the Google OAuth client; Google sign-in is on once it and the client secret are both set. 1–512 printable ASCII characters, no spaces.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_AUTH_X_CLIENT_ID: Client ID of the X OAuth 2.0 app; X sign-in is on once it and the client secret are both set. 1–512 printable ASCII characters, no spaces.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_AUTH_APPLE_SERVICES_ID: Services ID for Sign in with Apple (letters, digits, dots and hyphens); Apple sign-in needs it together with the team ID, key ID and private key.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_AUTH_APPLE_TEAM_ID: Team ID of the Apple developer account: 10 characters, A–Z and 0–9.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_AUTH_APPLE_KEY_ID: Key ID of the Sign in with Apple private key: 10 characters, A–Z and 0–9.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_AUTH_PASSKEYS: Passkey sign-in, on or off. Default: on as soon as any provider is configured.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_AUTH_PASSKEY_SIGNUP: Whether a visitor may create an account with a passkey alone, without a provider: on or off. Default off; needs passkeys on.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_AUTH_PASSKEY_SIGNUP_DAILY: Most passkey-only sign-ups per UTC day, all visitors together. 1–1000000, default 200.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_AUTH_PASSKEY_SIGNUP_INTERVAL: After three in a row, one passkey-only sign-up per client address per this interval. 1s–24h, default 1h.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_AUTH_MAX_PASSKEYS: Most passkeys one account may register. 1–100, default 20.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_AUTH_SESSION_IDLE: A session unused this long ends; nday auth-gc removes such sessions. 10m–365d, default 14d, never longer than NDAY_AUTH_SESSION_MAX.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_AUTH_SESSION_MAX: Longest a session lasts from sign-in, however active it is. 1h–400d, default 60d.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_AUTH_SENSITIVE_WINDOW: Sensitive actions (adding a passkey, linking an identity, deleting the account, every back-office action) need a sign-in at most this old. 1m–24h, default 15m.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_AUTH_HANDLE_HOLD: How long a released handle stays reserved for its previous owner. 0–3650d, default 90d.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_TERMS_VERSION: Version of the community rules in force (A–Z a–z 0–9 . _ -, at most 64 characters); posting needs it accepted. Empty: nothing to accept.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_AUTH_GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET: Client secret of the GitHub OAuth app, paired with NDAY_AUTH_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_AUTH_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET: Client secret of the Google OAuth client, paired with NDAY_AUTH_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_AUTH_X_CLIENT_SECRET: Client secret of the X OAuth 2.0 app, paired with NDAY_AUTH_X_CLIENT_ID.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_AUTH_APPLE_KEY: Private key for Sign in with Apple: the full PEM text of the .p8 file.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_HOT_PIN_MAX: Most CVEs pinned at the top of the hot list. When the rule below pins fewer, the rest is filled from the top of the discussed ranking. 0–20, default 10; 0 switches pinning off, fill included.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_HOT_PIN_RESEARCHERS: A CVE is pinned only when at least this many different researchers posted about it in the last 7 days (the @N badge). 1–100, default 2.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_HOT_PIN_RECENT_HOURS: …and its most recent researcher post is at most this many hours old. 1–168, default 72.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_HOT_PIN_WAVE_DAYS: …and its current wave of posts began at most this many days ago. A wave ends at a silence longer than this many days, so a CVE discussed again later can be pinned again. 1–30, default 7.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_CORRECTIONS_DAILY: Most corrections a user may report in 24 hours. 1–100000, default 10.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_CORRECTIONS_OPEN_PER_VULN: Most corrections waiting for an editor on one vulnerability, all readers together. 1–100000, default 20.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_CORRECTIONS_OPEN_PER_USER: Most corrections one user may have waiting on one vulnerability. 1–100000, default 3.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_CORRECTIONS_BURST: Correction requests a user may send in a burst, whatever the outcome. 1–100000, default 3.
admin.set.desc.NDAY_CORRECTIONS_EVERY: After the burst, one more correction request per this interval (e.g. 1m, 30s, 1d). 1ms–30d, default 1m.
